title: Registered or donated?
hook: Do donor-registration rates tell us the actual donation gap?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Separate a participation proxy from the downstream clinical outcome in country comparisons.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Separate a participation proxy from the downstream clinical outcome in country comparisons.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: In a toy population, 90% register and 20% of registered people complete the outcome. What fraction of the whole population completes it? Toy inputs A=[90, 20]; B=[50, 25].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[90, 18, 20], [50, 12.5, 25]]. Labels: Registered %, Donated %, Conditional %.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: A registration rate is an intermediate measure. Multiplying it by completion among registrants gives the downstream rate in this toy process. A larger registration gap need not translate into an equally large outcome gap.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Registered %=50, Conversion %=25. What is Donated %? Answer: 12.5.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Registered %=50, Conversion %=25. What is Donated %?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 12.5. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Presumed-consent countries have roughly 25–30% higher actual donation rates, a smaller gap than registration suggests (Abadie & Gay, 2006).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Separate a participation proxy from the downstream clinical outcome in country comparisons.
